Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit, TypeScript overrides on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`). I'm planning a full overhaul of the Storybook stories for the `ZimmProductCard` organism — read-only investigation, no edits.

Read and report back on, in full detail:

1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — the component's full contract: every prop it accepts, the full `VARIATION_CONFIG` object (all flags for each of the `home`/`plp`/`wishlist` variations — e.g. `showBag`, `showSizeChips`, `showBadge`, `showHoverImageSwap`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `hoverRevealsNotifyMe`, `sizeSelectorUnavailable`, `hideBagOnMobile`, and any others actually present — don't rely on this list, read the real file), how `isUnavailable` and any notify-me logic is derived/wired, and any other conditional rendering logic in the component body (e.g. how it decides to show a carousel vs single image, how badge label is chosen, how bag-hide-on-mobile-when-unavailable — if present — is computed).

2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` — list every named export (story) currently in this file, and for each one, what props/state it renders (variation, unavailable, badge, multi-image, sale price, one-size, etc.) — a table would help. Note the `title` used for the Storybook category and any `play` functions.

3. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/` — list every file in this folder (stories, tests, anything else), and for the stories file specifically, list every named export the same way as #2, plus figure out and report what organizing principle it currently uses (the repo's own `plan.md` describes it as "a per-Figma-node coverage folder" — confirm what that means concretely by reading the file: are exports named/grouped by Figma node ID? By AC number? Something else?). Note whether this folder's stories overlap in content with the main `index.stories.tsx` ones from #2, and whether the two use different or the same Storybook `title`/category.

4. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` — do NOT read this file in full (it's very large), but run `grep -n "^  test(\|^    test(\|describe(" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` and report the list of test/describe names, so I can see what state/behavior combinations are already covered at the unit-test layer (stories shouldn't need to duplicate what's already proven there — they're for visual/interaction review, not logic proof).

5. Also check whether anything else in the repo imports from or references the `nodeCoverage` folder (`grep -rn "nodeCoverage" overrides/ .storybook/ 2>/dev/null`), so I know if deleting it is fully isolated or has other consumers.

6. For comparison/precedent: briefly check one or two sibling files that also have many prop-driven states — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.stories.tsx` and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/index.stories.tsx` — just list their named exports (one line each), to see the house style for "one file, many named-export states" without a separate coverage folder.

Report everything as structured findings (tables/lists), not prose narrative. I'm going to use this to design a consolidated story structure, so precision on prop values per existing story matters more than summarization.

375	  const intl = useIntl();
376	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];

378	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback

384	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
385	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the

391	  //
392	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
393	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
394	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
395	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
396	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
397	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
398	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
399	  //
400	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
401	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
402	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
403	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
404	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
405	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
406	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
407	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
408	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
